summary: Verified all 3 reported issues. (1) MOBILE Provider Price Checker — Service dropdown is Title-Cased (31 options, joining words 'and'/'or' lowercase, e.g. 'Allied Health and Other Therapeutic Services', 'Counsellor or Psychotherapist'); 'Service' and 'Rate charged (…)' labels show '(required)'; Provider label is exactly 'Provider' with helper text 'Pre-filled from your account. Edit if this rate is from a different provider.' and NO '(optional)' text. (2) MOBILE InsightGraphics donut now uses <G transform=`rotate(-90 x y)`> instead of transform-origin; grep across /app/mobile/src returns ZERO occurrences of 'transform-origin' or 'transformOrigin'. Console scan on the Expo preview after loading Price Checker, Statement Decoder, Decoded Statements screens produced 0 'transform-origin'/'Invalid DOM property' entries. (3) BACKEND trial reminders — POST /api/internal/trial-tick returned 200 {"midtrial_sent":0,"final_nudge_sent":0,"reminders_sent":0,"expired_handled":0}, no real Resend emails sent (no trialing subs in the window). Code inspection of _process_trial_reminders_once in server.py confirms exactly ONE live reminder block ('Two days left in your Wayly trial', window trial_ends_at in [now+36h, now+2d]) plus the post-expiry 'Your Wayly trial has ended' notice. No '$', 'Solo is', 'Family is', 'One day left' or 'ends today' strings in either live body (all '$' matches in the function are Mongo operators). routes/payments.py 'customer.subscription.trial_will_end' branch is a pass (no email).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Did not force a real decoded-statement/invoice detail render in the mobile preview (login selector mismatch sent me to /decoded-statements → Unmatched Route). The transform-origin fix is nonetheless proven safe by grep (zero occurrences in /app/mobile/src) and by a clean console across price-checker + statement-decoder + decoded-statements routes. If you want visual donut proof, log in as cathy@example.com manually in the Expo preview and open any saved statement/invoice; testIDs are 'statement-graphics' and 'invoice-graphics'.
rca of the issue: SVG donut was passing rotation via <G rotation={-90} origin='x,y'> which react-native-svg on web renders as the CSS prop 'transform-origin' (hyphenated) — React logs 'Invalid DOM property transform-origin. Did you mean transformOrigin?'. Fix: pass a single transform string <G transform={`rotate(-90 ${cx} ${cy})`}>, which react-native-svg converts to a valid SVG attribute and bypasses the warning.
